messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: a mixture-model expression in Stan
parts:
Hi all. I was corresponding with someone who was trying to use Stan for models with discrete parameters, using the mixture model formulation as explained in the manual. He felt that the log-probability specification was hard for users in his subfield to understand. This made me think, maybe we could add a new distribution called finite_mixture or something like that, where the arguments are the probabilities and the mixture distributions. I’m not quite sure how this would be done—to do it in sufficient generality to be useful might end up being even more complicated to use—but I just wanted to throw this idea out there.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] a mixture-model expression in Stan
parts:
On Mar 1, 2014, at 7:16 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

> Hi all. I was corresponding with someone who was trying to use Stan for models with discrete parameters, using the mixture model formulation as explained in the manual. He felt that the log-probability specification was hard for users in his subfield to understand. This made me think, maybe we could add a new distribution called finite_mixture or something like that, where the arguments are the probabilities and the mixture distributions. I'm not quite sure how this would be done--to do it in sufficient generality to be useful might end up being even more complicated to use--but I just wanted to throw this idea out there.

I added an issue to which you (or others) can comment on GitHub:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/583

I can't quite tell what you're thinking of in terms of a concrete
syntax. Something like a distribution:

y ~ finite_mixture(lambda,
normal(mu1,sigma1),
normal(mu2,sigma2),
normal(mu3,sigma3));

for a three-way mixture where lambda is a 3-simplex and so on?
Or something more like a function, as in:

increment_log_prob(finite_mixture(lambda,
normal_log(y,mu1,sigma1),
normal_log(y,mu2,sigma2),
normal_log(y,mu3,sigma3)));

We can be pretty flexible with things in the modeling language,
so that we could take any number of arguments for something like
this.

But I've been having a hard time seeing how we could parameterize
all this. Especially if we have vector parmaeters y, mu or sigma.

Mixtures aren't the only case we want to deal with when marginalizing
out discrete params, but we could perhaps start there.

And what's the priority for this, if any? You've told me recently not
to bother with adding new distributions and to let users do it, but
this is going to be much trickier because it's not a usual function
or distribution but something that needs to be finessed in the
modeling language for a flexible syntax.

- Bob
